title.narrative: Provision of immediate life-saving WASH response and durable, cost-effective water supply in recurrent emergency hotspot rural areas of Baidoa.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtErratic weather, struggle for dwindling resources, exacerbating poverty, new and protracted armed conflicts continue to drive Somali rural agro pastoral communities away from their homes and into overcrowded towns and cities.lt/spangt ltfont face="Arial, sans-serif" color="#000000"gtThe cumulative effects of the five consecutive below-average rainy seasons have resulted in a sharp forecasted increase in humanitarian needs across all sectors, particularly in WASH, Health Nutrition. According to the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) Somalia, 2023 : Rural households mostly depend on open or unprotected water sources or water sources that are susceptible to drought such as shallow wells and water pans. Approximately 80 per cent of the rural population access water through a dam or pond which increases the risk of water-borne diseases such as diarrhea. In addition only 4 per cent of the rural households living in Bay region agro-pastoral areas have access to safe water. Poor WASH and health conditions drive the increased rates of malnutrition. The WASH cluster aims to protect lives while ensuring the provision of sustainable and cost-effective WASH services to affected communities in the affected rural areas, in the spirit of sector integration COOPI conducted a joint needs assessment with Somalia Cash Consortium in hard to reach villages of rural Baidoa and Identified the current immediate needs in regard to drought displacements impact mitigation measures. The survey recommended ongoing coordination to plan immediate response measures with WASH cluster, Nutrition and Health. In this light, COOPI proposes to reach 19134 people who include 5357 women,5358 girls,3253 men and 5166 boys
emergency with sustainable solutions to reduce mortality and morbidity while offering dignity. The target location is 9 affected host rural villages in Baidoa as follows Durow,Midow,Moshe,Masubiye,Goof galooli,Bula robow,Qahir winey,Aburow and Kashidow. The proposed emergency activities are distribution of 1500 hygiene kits to the most vulnerable to malnutrition from South West State regional hub to the hard-to-reach rural Baidoa, surface and household water treatment and quality monitoring followed by more sustainable improvement and sustainable expansion existing three multi use boreholes in Midow, Qahir winey and Aburow rural villages as well as capacity building the Water Management Committees. The target water points are strategic boreholes whose capacity will be increased to provide safe water to neighboring villages of Moshe and Masubiye. through construction of elevated storage tanks to enhance storage and pressures, upgrading to solar pumping to reduce operation fuel costs, pipeline extensions as well as construction of masonry water kiosks for water access. COOPI has ongoing livelihood projects in rural Baidoa funded by ECHO and SomReP, the presence will serve as an entry point for the field staff in particular during identification of community mobilisers to conduct participatory hygiene and sanitation promotion at the villages. According to WHO Diarrhea disease is the second leading cause of death in children under five years old whereas it is both preventable and treatable. COOPI will work closely with the Ministry of Health and Nutrition partners based in Baidoa to reduce the deprivation of children of the nutrition necessary for growth as diarrhea is a major cause of malnutrition, and malnourished children are more likely to fall ill from diarrhea. lt/fontgtlt/pgt
